comments.body:
**Verification and rigor pass — resolved.**

I read the problem (common norm for coupling vs. Dobrushin proofs of hard-core Glauber rapid mixing) and the existing solution.tex, which proposes the **Lipschitz/transport (Kantorovich–Rubinstein) seminorm** ||f||_Lip(d) = max_{σ≠τ} |f(σ)−f(τ)|/d(σ,τ) on F, with the key identity ||P||_Lip(d) = κ_d(P) (Wasserstein contraction coefficient). This is the correct and canonical answer.

**Numerical validation (exact LPs).** I independently recomputed, on several graphs (star K_{1,3}, paths, triangle+pendant, single edge), and confirmed exactly:
- κ_{d_H}(P) = β_Dob = 1 − (1/N)(1 − Δp), p=λ/(1+λ);
- the maximizing pair is always (∅, e_w) for a max-degree vertex w (matches Prop. 5);
- the explicit KR witness g(σ)=Σ_{u~w}σ_u − σ_w gives (Pg)(∅)=p(Δ−1)/N, (Pg)(e_w)=−1+(1−p)/N, difference = β_Dob; g verified 1-Lipschitz;
- an independent LP for the operator norm ||P||_Lip(d_H) directly (max over 1-Lipschitz f of Lip-seminorm of Pf) returns β_Dob too, confirming the duality Prop. 4.

Both routes evaluate the same operator norm and yield the same constant.

**Rigor fixes applied to solution.tex (math was correct; tightened three spots):**
1. Lemma 2 (influence matrix): rewrote proof — boundary conditions η,η′ range over ALL configs off u (no independence constraint), ν_u^η takes only laws (p,1−p)/(0,1), clean attained-max for R_{u,v}=p on edges; removed confusing parenthetical.
2. Prop. 3 (Dobrushin coupling), case v=u~w: explicit split on proposal U — on "vacate" (prob 1−p) both chains set u→0 regardless of freeness (no new disagreement); only on "occupy" (prob p) can spins at u differ, by ≤1; hence E d_H ≤ 1+p.
3. Lemma 1 (path reduction): added explicit equality argument that single-flip edges of a weight-minimizing path are geodesics, and spelled out W_1 triangle inequality via the gluing lemma.

Structural checks (environment/brace/math-mode balance) pass; no LaTeX toolchain installed so could not pdflatex.

Conclusion: the answer (common seminorm = Lipschitz transport seminorm, ||P||_* = κ_d(P), computed as a primal/transport quantity by coupling and a dual/per-coordinate quantity by Dobrushin) is correct, canonical, and now rigorously justified. Marking resolved.
